subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The English word "tsunami" comes from the Japanese words "tsu" (harbor) and "nami" (wave).
• Today, dozens of countries use early warning systems to detect tsunamis.
• Indonesia operates the Indonesian Tsunami Early Warning System.
prompt: The student wants to provide an example of a country that operates a tsunami warning system. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The Japanese words "tsu" and "nami" are the origin of the English word "tsunami."
choices.B: Today, several countries operate systems designed to detect and warn populations about tsunamis.
choices.C: Indonesia operates the Indonesian Tsunami Early Warning System as its national detection network.
choices.D: Indonesia does not rely on the Japanese word "tsunami" in naming its warning system.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it directly accomplishes the goal by providing a specific, concrete example of a country operating a tsunami warning system. Drawing from the third note in the list, this choice names both the country (Indonesia) and its specific warning system (the Indonesian Tsunami Early Warning System). This level of specificity is exactly what the question requests—an example that illustrates the general point about countries operating such systems. The sentence effectively synthesizes information from the notes into a clear, focused statement that achieves the stated objective.
